Free Write is a typewriter for text and a sketch pad for drawing; `instrument` is which one the page is now. TEXT by default and not persisted (session-scoped): a page that remembered INK would open unable to type.

what this mode lets the writer do to the page's ink, derived from mode and instrument, never stored: Free Write is `edit` in INK and `inert` in TEXT; Draft and Revise are `movable`. The ternary reaches `movable` only past `mode === 'journal'`, so Free Write can never acquire it by accident.

persist strokes, merging the LIVE text so a pending typed run is never clobbered (Free Write's text autosave is debounced). An unborn page has no row and a stroke is content: the row is written WITH the ink in one synchronous act (`birthWith`), never created empty first; an ink-only page is not empty.

The heading line the floating +/- sits beside, as plain offsets from the last full recompute. A scroll changes nothing the recompute derives, so it only re-places the pop, while one is shown, at most once a frame (the full recompute reads the whole page's innerText, and the typewriter scrolls on every line).

The floating +/-: shown only while a selection sits on a heading line, placed where it never covers a word (past the heading's last line, else in the column's left margin); a fixed overlay, so the page never moves.

the Draft-open typewriter is decided once at mount (empty deps freeze `mode` and `initialText`; the component remounts per page, so a mode switch within one mount never re-runs it); an EMPTY page opens with the typewriter OFF, having no lines to follow

This hook sits ABOVE the early return below (the hooks-order guards enforce it); its body reads `applyFormatAt`, defined below, safely, since an effect runs after render, and its deps carry `!!realEntry` so the listener attaches once the editor mounts. Tab indents through draftFormat's own indent (a leading tab), the same formatter as the rail's arrows, so a key and a click cannot drift apart. It is a state machine (store/tabChord.ts): each Tab tap is one more first-line level, Shift+Tab one back, Tab held + 1 one whole-paragraph level per press; a tap applies on release, and a quick Tab-then-1 types its 1. Draft and Revise act everywhere; Free Write is forward-only, so it acts on a BLANK line only and never outdents. Capturing Tab costs a keyboard-only writer Tab-out; Escape leaves the surface (store/escapeExit.ts). While an Outline is in Draft it owns Tab and this machine stands aside (a ref, read at press time).
the durable-relationship doors: pairing, porting and pinning outlive the visit, so they birth the page FIRST and then act on the real row, as one act: no dangling pointer, no orphan

The template picker (Sliver, Templates; Draft and later strips, never Free Write): Blank, Screenplay, Outline, Title Page, Bibliography. The host owns the act: an EMPTY page (no words, no ink) takes the choice in place; a page WITH words or ink never moves, and the choice opens a NEW page in the same home, whose chip reads "Opened as a new page · Back". Pressing the current choice changes nothing. A template is a lens set through patchPageSettings, as `kind` is; on an unborn page it rides the address.

scales with --paper-scale so the editor's type grows with the paper (the measure is the constant, not the pixel width); it reaches the contenteditable by inheritance (ForwardOnlyEditor spreads this style on its outer wrap). A page's default is 12 real points in page units (index.css --wz-pt).

the ink stratum paints OVER the text (a later sibling: ink under type would be hidden). It renders in every mode, since the ink is the page's, framed only (below 1100px the page keeps its pre-ink terms). Mode varies permission, not presence (`inkPermission`); both canvases stay pointer-events:none and routing belongs to the sheet.

The rail's Bold/Italic/Heading/Spacing tools act on entry.text directly (markdown conventions, no separate rich-text state): read the selection by linear offset (store/caretOffset.ts), transform (store/draftFormat.ts), then re-decorate through ForwardOnlyEditor's own guarded helper (decorateEditorFor), never a bare innerHTML write, which would bring back Chromium's trailing-newline caret quirk; a rail click and a keystroke leave the same state. One implementation, two gates: `applyRailFormat`'s `mode !== 'drafting'` guard keeps a leaked Revise rail inert, so each caller brings its own scope (the rail Draft-only, Tab in Draft and Revise).
